props.gloss_en: R' Abba and Rav Huna bar Chiyya, asked by Levi bar Shmuel about reassembling a weavers' bed on Shabbat: it is fine
Rav and Shmuel: one who reassembles a weavers' bed on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering
one who puts back a candelabrum's branch on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering
a plasterers' pole -- he should not put it back; if he did, he is exempt, but it is forbidden
R' Simai: a rounded horn -- liable
R' Simai: a straight horn -- exempt
the baraita: bed-frames, bed-legs and archers' boards -- he should not put them back; if he did, he is exempt, but it is forbidden
...and he should not fasten [them]; if he fastened, he is liable to a sin-offering
RSBG: if it was loose, it is permitted
the first tanna: reassembling them is forbidden [even where exempt]
Rav Chama's household had a collapsible bed and would reassemble it on Yom Tov
Rava: I hold like RSBG, who said that if it is loose it is permitted
